transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir P., Lena O., Noah K. (Redwood) — Jules C., Priya M., Marcus L., Talia G. (AstraLogic)

Auto-summary (auto-generated may be noisy): go over ttft and stream; discuss kernel fallback and sequence len sampling.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): Alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly POC sync for AstraLogic latency pilot. Today we'll run through the latest numbers, and then propose a kernel prioritization. Can everyone hear me okay?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Jules): Yeah, we can hear you. Thanks.
00:12 Speaker 1 (Samir): Sweet. Quick agenda: TTFT outliers, streaming handshake and first-token path, sequence length buckets, and then kernel choices.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Lena): I sent the spreadsheet earlier, it's the microburst sampling sheet, might be labelled "latency-breakdown-v3" in the drive.
00:33 Speaker 4 (Priya): Got it, I opened it. Quick note, our staging workload has a heavier tail after the 512 token bin, so seqlen mix is a little skewed.
00:45 Speaker 1 (Samir): Okay that explains some of the 99th perc spikes. Marcus, from infra side any new observations?
00:50 Speaker 5 (Marcus): Yeah so we've seen recurring ~120-200ms hiccups that align with GC events on the batch router and then a bunch of small 20-40ms microbursts. The bigger ones correlate with system-level context switches when the node is under memory pressure.
01:10 Speaker 6 (Talia): Are those the 'microbursts' we've been talking about? Because product is concerned about user experience on streaming.
01:18 Speaker 3 (Lena): Right, and streaming makes those very visible because the first-byte path is sensitive to handshake jitter. In the traces we re-ran, when the prefix cache hit rates drop the first-token path degenerates to a slower kernel.
01:36 Speaker 2 (Jules): Quick question — can Redwood toggle fallback to the lower-latency quantized variant automatically when load spikes?
01:42 Speaker 1 (Samir): We have a hedging/fallback policy available. The tricky bit is model variant compatibility for some of your prompt types; we need to ensure quality delta is acceptable. We'll show the quality checks we ran.
01:55 Speaker 4 (Priya): On quality, we saw a few hallucination-ish completions in the 8-bit run on long prompts, especially with code-like inputs. Not a showstopper but worth noting.
02:08 Speaker 3 (Lena): That's expected, quantization impacts are more visible on longer seqlen. For 1-256 tokens quantized path looked reasonable in our evals.
02:20 Speaker 5 (Marcus): Can we talk about batcher knobs? Right now our batch size target is 8 and max waiting time is 15ms, that seems to increase latency variance.
02:34 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yeah those are tunables — in the last run we tried batch target 4 and max wait 10ms and saw improved TTFT at the cost of throughput. We can trade.
02:46 Speaker 6 (Talia): Product's requirement is 95p under 300ms for streaming first byte — is that feasible without dedicated?
02:54 Speaker 3 (Lena): It's borderline for hosted unless we apply more aggressive caching and a smaller batch target; dedicated would give you more headroom.
03:06 Speaker 2 (Jules): Pricing tradeoffs come into play there.
03:09 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yup. We'll include cost delta in the spreadsheet.
03:12 Speaker 4 (Priya): I also flagged a test where a 2k token prompt caused a kernel fallback mid-stream and spiked to 1.2s for a few tokens, so that creates a bad user perception.
03:25 Speaker 3 (Lena): If a long seqlen enters mid-request, we can hedge: spawn a faster kernel for the first token while continuing on the standard path, then switch over if quality holds. That's more of a runtime hack but we've prototyped it.
03:40 Speaker 5 (Marcus): Sounds complex. How do we validate correctness?
03:44 Speaker 1 (Samir): We'll run A/B on the prompt set Priya shares; Lena will put together a regression harness.
03:50 Speaker 2 (Jules): Ok. For the TTFT outliers, I uploaded three sample traces, one labeled "trace_gc_05-16" — those show the GC alignment.
04:00 Speaker 3 (Lena): I pulled those; interestingly the KV cache eviction pattern lines up with the microburst. The recorder spelled it as "kayvee" in the notes, so apologies for the ASR noise.
04:12 Speaker 4 (Priya): Can Redwood take a look at our VPC egress metrics? We think some of the extra latency stems from cross-subnet routing.
04:20 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yes, Marcus, please share egress subnets and we can correlate. We'll need redacted logs to be safe.
04:27 Speaker 5 (Marcus): Will do.
04:30 Speaker 1 (Samir): Okay let's jump to kernel prioritization — Lena, you want to walk through the table?
04:35 Speaker 3 (Lena): Sure. We propose primary fastpath = conv-attn kernel variant, fallback to q4-json quant path, second fallback to the generic fused kernel. The priority also differs by seqlen bucket: under 256 prefer fastpath; 256-1024 prefer quant-hedge; above 1024 prefer fused with async streaming.
05:00 Speaker 6 (Talia): Can you explain conv-attn, I'm not sure product knows what that implies for dev experience.
05:06 Speaker 3 (Lena): Conv-attn is our optimized kernel for short contexts — it reduces per-token latency by ~15-25ms in our bench. It's transparent at the API layer.
05:15 Speaker 4 (Priya): Is there any model architecture sensitivity? Our model is a hybrid with local attention tweaks.
05:21 Speaker 3 (Lena): We validated on a few local variants; tracker showed minor diffs. We'll include the compatibility matrix.
05:30 Speaker 2 (Jules): How does this interact with streaming? If the first token uses conv-attn but subsequent tokens don't, will we see jank?
05:38 Speaker 3 (Lena): Potentially, yes. That's why we recommend hedging only for the initial handshake and then reconciling to the best-effort path.
05:47 Speaker 1 (Samir): Ok I'm going to note an experiment: 24-hour replay with batch target 4, conv-attn primary, quant fallback with quality gating. We'll measure 50/95/99 and streaming FTB.
06:00 Speaker 5 (Marcus): What's the rollback plan if quality regresses in production?
06:05 Speaker 1 (Samir): Canary on small percentage of requests, with automatic rollback if the quality metric (per-sample perplexity delta + business prompt checks) fails the threshold. We'll script that.
06:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): Can you share the quality checklist?
06:22 Speaker 3 (Lena): Yes — I'll add the checklist to the doc: sample prompts, gold outputs, fuzzy match thresholds.
06:30 Speaker 2 (Jules): Also, can we get a separate run with longer seqlen heavy tails to see stability?
06:36 Speaker 1 (Samir): Yes, Priya's seqlen export will be used for that.
06:41 Speaker 6 (Talia): A small ask from product — if we can trim visible spikes for end-users we can tolerate slightly higher average latency. So focusing on 95/99p is good.
06:53 Speaker 3 (Lena): Noted.
07:00 Speaker 4 (Priya): One more note — we have compliance gating; before we run anything on dedicated or access logs we need SOC2 docs.
07:08 Speaker 1 (Samir): We'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts. Noah, can you drop the link to the secure intake?
07:13 Speaker 6 (Noah): Yep I'll send the secure intake form and the SOC2 bucket.
07:17 Speaker 5 (Marcus): Timeline check — we want to be able to decide on dedicated vs hosted by end of month. Is that realistic?
07:24 Speaker 1 (Samir): It's tight but doable if we get the microburst replay and the canary results within two weeks.
07:31 Speaker 3 (Lena): We'll prioritize the microburst replay first, then the hedging experiment.
07:36 Speaker 4 (Priya): Who owns the replay orchestration?
07:39 Speaker 1 (Samir): Redwood will own the replay (Samir/Lena), Marcus will provide traces.
07:45 Speaker 2 (Jules): OK thanks.
07:48 Speaker 6 (Talia): Quick question on cost — if we reduce batch size to 4, roughly what's the expected CPU/GPU cost increase?
07:55 Speaker 3 (Lena): Ballpark 12-20% more GPU time for the same qps; but cost per perceived user is lower because latency is better. We'll add exact numbers to the sheet.
08:08 Speaker 1 (Samir): Alright let's capture the explicit next steps then.
08:12 Speaker 2 (Jules): I'll follow up with a short email that contains the priority list and the three critical traces.
08:18 Speaker 3 (Lena): And I'll update the kernel priority tab.
08:22 Speaker 5 (Marcus): I'll upload the redacted microburst logs to the shared S3 link.
08:27 Speaker 6 (Noah): I'll post SOC2 and intake form links to the thread.
08:33 Speaker 4 (Priya): Sound good. Thanks everyone.
08:36 Speaker 1 (Samir): Thanks all — we'll reconvene same time next week unless you need an earlier sync.

End of transcript.
